featured_reviews.review_text: Best Buryanii Yet ... anyTime calcutta is not just known for histories... they have the bestest taste ever 💜❤️ & finally we found Streets Of Calcutta 💜❤️ Same Taste., Same Vibe., Same Atmosphere.., People Of Mumbai Visit Atleast Once & Experience The Taste Of Streets Of Calcutta 💜❤️ & It Has Breakfast Items As Well., Dal Puri & Many More The Best 💜❤️

featured_reviews.name: Antara Trivedi
featured_reviews.review_text: Streets of Calcutta is now renewed at a spacious location in just opposite lane of its previous location, However one thing remains unchanged is the quality, taste and flavour of the food they serve. While they serve it exactly like kolkata, this place will always be close to your heart once you visit here. The puchkas are to die for. Makes you super nostalgic. The sone pe suhaga is just how fresh their food is. The drinks and the desserts are a plus on how good the food is. Must must visit. They have heard you people, with ample seating and beautiful ambience and finger licking food, they are back!!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Antara, Thank you so much for your lovely review!
We’re happy to know that while we’ve moved to a more spacious location, the taste, quality, and flavours you love remain the same. It means a lot that our food brought back those Kolkata-style nostalgic vibes, especially the phuchkas!
We’re glad you enjoyed the fresh food, drinks, desserts, seating, and ambience. Looking forward to welcoming you back again soon for more finger-licking Bengali delicacies.
Regards, Team Streets of Calcutta

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Streets of Calcutta is located on the main Oshiwara road and it is easy to find.

The seating is very limited hence call and confirm before visiting as mostly it is a takeaway outlet. I guess 4 people can sit inside.

The menu is Bengali cuisine and its super authentic. The menu is simple yet it offer variety. Prices are not high and quantity served is huge. Also they serve authentic in house made puchkas which was like the best that I have had apart from the ones which you get everywhere.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Chicken Moghlai Paratha with Aloor Dom -
One of the super heavy appetisers that you would come accept. Thick crispy paratha generously filled with minced chicken tasted perfect. Loved the taste of the filling as it had nice amount of spices used. The potato served along was also good but the paratha is a meal in itself.

MAINS~
Chicken Kosha with Luchi -
Chicken gravy with big version of puri tasted good. Again the gravy was flavourful and the puri was the best.

Veg Special Thali -
The veg thali consisted of all the below items and everything was really good. Loved eating everything in it.
Luchi, Aloor Dom, Dal Rice, Vegetable Curry, Crispy Veg Chop, Tangy Chutney, Mishti Doi.

So our meal at Streets of Calcutta Oshiwara was good however I wish they come up with a bigger outlet so we can enjoy the perfect dining experience.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Shaikh
We’re thrilled to hear you enjoyed your visit to Streets of Calcutta and appreciated the authenticity of our Bengali cuisine! Thank you for highlighting the Chicken Moghlai Paratha and the Veg Special Thali; your descriptions make our dishes sound even more inviting. We genuinely appreciate your feedback regarding our seating capacity, and we hope to enhance your dining experience in the future.
Regards, Team Streets of Calcutta

featured_reviews.name: Sharmin Hazarika
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Streets of Calcutta for the second time. It’s a nice, cozy place that’s ideal for families looking to enjoy Bengali cuisine. My first visit was quite pleasant, which is why we decided to return.

During this visit, we ordered four fish thalis, a Basanti Pulao, Chicken Kosha, chutney, and two appetizers. Unfortunately, the service was a bit slow. The appetizers were tasty but one of the fish thalis was served undercooked, which we brought to the staff’s attention and requested to be replaced. There was no apt piece available so packed one piece of chicken as replacement.

Also, they don’t provide glass with plates.

While the ambiance and food are generally enjoyable, I hope the kitchen pays more attention to the cooking quality and service speed to ensure a consistently good experience.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Sharmin, We truly appreciate your continued trust in us and are glad to know that you find our restaurant cozy and family-friendly for enjoying Bengali cuisine.
That said, we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience you faced during your recent visit. The delay in service and the issue with the undercooked fish thali is certainly not the experience we aim to provide. While we are glad our team tried to offer a replacement, we understand that it was not an ideal solution, and we take your feedback very seriously. We have shared this with our kitchen and service team to ensure better quality checks and improved service speed going forward.
Your note about the glass not being provided with plates has also been considered, and we will work on improving this aspect of the dining experience.
Thank you once again for your honest feedback—it truly helps us improve. We hope you’ll give us another opportunity to serve you better and provide you with the consistently enjoyable experience you expect from Streets of Calcutta.
Regards, Team Streets of Calcutta

featured_reviews.name: Aman SharmaJii
featured_reviews.review_text:
Streets of Calcutta is a decent spot if you're craving Bengali street food in Mumbai. The star of the visit was definitely the Puchka - absolutely amazing! It had the perfect flavour and left a lingering aftertaste that reminded me of Kolkata.

I also tried their Dal Kachori with Dum Aloo, but it felt more like a big Dal Puri than an actual kachori. The taste was okay - nothing special, just decent.

Overall, if you're from Bengal or Odisha and missing those familiar flavours, their Puchka and Jhal Muri will definitely hit the right notes. Simple place, but worth it for the taste of home.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Aman
We're delighted to hear that you enjoyed our Puchka and found it reminiscent of Kolkata! It's always rewarding to know that we can bring a taste of home to our guests. We appreciate your feedback on the Dal Kachori with Dum Aloo, and we will certainly take it into consideration as we continue to refine our menu.
Regards, Team Streets of Calcutta

featured_reviews.name: Irom Lamjingba
featured_reviews.review_text:
We ordered Fish Thali, Chicken Dagbangla, Dal with Egg Tadka, Basanti Pulao,luchi but the overall experience was extremely disappointing.

The fish in the thali was uncooked and the jhol was completely tasteless. Begun Bhaja seemed to be fried in contaminated oil, the dal was too bland, and the quantity of aloo jhuri was very less. Chicken Dagbangla was again tasteless with undercooked chicken and sweet.

After taking our order for Dal with Egg Tadka and Phulka Roti, the staff informed us after almost 19 minutes that roti was not available. Chicken Biryani was also unavailable. The staff insisted we try Basanti Pulao instead, but it was not good at all.

Service and staff behaviour were poor throughout. Even after requesting a refill for the aloo jhuri, there was no response for a long time, though they eventually refilled it.

Lastly, and most importantly, the restaurant is located next to a dump yard, which raises serious hygiene concerns.

Overall, a very bad experience. Definitely not recommended, and I will never visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

featured_reviews.name: Arshad Mir
featured_reviews.review_text:
Brunched at MAG St. Bandra recently and as someone who’s eaten through enough of Bombay’s brunch circuit to know when a place is pure hype versus when there’s actual substance behind the aesthetic — MAG St definitely falls in the latter category. The food is genuinely good. The problem? They’ve started pricing like they’re in Notting Hill or Le Marais.

Started strong with the watermelon feta salad — fresh, balanced and properly refreshing, though ice-cold watermelon would’ve taken it up another notch in Bombay heat. The dim sums were fair play overall. The truffle edamame dumplings were decent but forgettable, while the shrimp in ginger broth dumplings were the clear standout. That broth/sauce situation was excellent.

The Asian fried rice was honestly a surprise hit. Comforting, flavourful, generous enough portion-wise — though realistically this is a ₹550 dish masquerading as an ₹825 one because Bandra brunch economics require everything to sound “premium” enough for the Bandra aunties and influencer crowd.

Then came the smoked salmon eggs benedict — the dish everyone seems to post here. It was alright. Not bad by any means, but I’ve definitely had better at Sarabeth's. The hollandaise was absolutely drenched over the eggs to the point it overpowered everything else a bit.

The real stars? The drinks. Phenomenal. Especially the Summer Thirst — probably the best thing we ordered all afternoon.

Bill came to around ₹5.4k for two (roughly £42 / €49), which honestly could and probably should have landed closer to ₹4k. But then again, this is Bandra in 2026 — people here are happily paying London and Paris brunch prices while sitting off Linking Road, so fair play to MAG St for understanding their market perfectly.

Overall: stylish spot, genuinely solid kitchen, not just Instagram fluff — but you’re definitely paying a Bandra premium on top of the food.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Arshad,
Thank you for such a thoughtful and detailed review. We truly appreciate the time you took to share your experience dish by dish - and we’re delighted to hear that the food, drinks, and overall experience resonated with you beyond just the aesthetic.

We’re especially glad the Summer Thirst, shrimp dumplings, and Asian fried rice stood out for you. Feedback like yours is always incredibly valuable to us.

We understand your thoughts on pricing as well. Perfectly crisp tikki loaded with flavorful chutneys and fresh curd. Every bite had the right balance of sweet, tangy, and spicy flavors. Truly satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Meghina Vaity
featured_reviews.review_text: Absolutely loved the food at Chaat Hauz! 😍 The chaats were super fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced with spices. The ambiance was clean, vibrant, and service was quick too. Definitely visiting again for more delicious bites! 🌮✨

featured_reviews.name: Prathamesh Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Had an amazing experience at Chaat Hauz in Khar! As someone who loves chaat, it's rare to find a place that gets every dish right, but this place absolutely delivered.
We started with the Palak Patta Chaat, and it was outstanding. The crispy spinach leaves, perfectly balanced chutneys, and crunchy toppings created an explosion of flavors and textures in every bite. Easily one of the best versions I've had in Mumbai.
The Ragda Pattice was equally impressive. The pattice was crisp on the outside and soft inside, while the ragda was flavorful and comforting without being overly spicy. It had that authentic street-food taste with a premium touch.
The Dahi Makhana Chaat was a pleasant surprise and probably the most unique dish of the lot. Light, refreshing, and beautifully balanced with creamy dahi and flavorful chutneys, it stood out from the usual chaat options available elsewhere.
The star of the evening was the Avocado Papdi Chaat. Such a creative fusion dish! The creamy avocado blended beautifully with the traditional chaat elements, creating something innovative without losing the essence of authentic Indian chaat.
The presentation of every dish was excellent, ingredients tasted fresh, portions were satisfying, and the service was warm and attentive. The restaurant has managed to give traditional chaat a modern twist while maintaining authentic flavors.
If you're a chaat lover looking for something beyond the ordinary, Chaat Hauz in Khar is definitely worth visiting. Every dish we tried was packed with flavor, creativity, and quality. Looking forward to coming back and exploring more of their menu. Highly recommended! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

featured_reviews.name: Zakiya Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: QFinally found the best chaat spot in Khar and Chaat Hauz completely lives up to the hype — every single item is a flavour bomb and you can taste the freshness in every bite. Started with their legendary pani puri where the puris were perfectly crisp and the teekha-khatta pudina pani had that perfect street-style kick that hits instantly, then moved to dahi batata puri which was insanely balanced with chilled sweet dahi, tangy chutneys, and aloo masala that just melts in your mouth without making the puri soggy at all. The sev puri had great crunch with fresh onion-tomato toppings and the ragda pattice was piping hot with buttery ragda, spicy chutneys, and loads of sev on top — proper Mumbai style. Even though it’s a small standing/takeaway setup with no seating, the counters are surprisingly clean, staff is super quick even during the 6-9pm rush, and hygiene is clearly a priority which is rare for street chaat places. Prices are very reasonable at ₹60-120 per plate and portions are generous, plus the bhaiya serving is polite and remembers regulars. If you’re craving authentic, no-nonsense Mumbai chaat that tastes exactly like it should, skip the fancy cafes and come straight here — Chaat Hauz is a Khar institution for a reason and I’m already planning my next visit for bhel and samosa chaat!

featured_reviews.name: TravelWithDev04
featured_reviews.review_text:
✅ Overall Experience: 5/5
We went there for lunch, it was 4 of us, we go for yearly Diwali lunch and it was a perfect place for that. The food was really awesome. Also the owner, who is a doctor is very passionate about food, and it shows.
The best part is food, even though fried, does not feel oily.

✅ Food: 5/5
We started with Dal Pakwan, which is a famous sindhi dish, and I have personally not had a great one so far, but this place has the perfect dal pakwan. We had two varieties of dal pakwan, Dal Pakwan and Ulhasnagar Dal Pakwan, and we loved the Ulhasnagar one more.
Starters: In starters we order Mix Tuk, it has fried potato and Arbi(Taro Root/ Colocasia). The Arbi was super awesome. The spices were so good that we asked them to give it to us separately with our chhanch.
Starters: We also ordered Sanna Pakora, which is Onion Pakora/Bhajiya. I liked the crunch of it, as it was a different take on it. One of the friend did not like it as much, because she wanted more Onions.
Mains: I personally love Sai Bhaji and we ordered it with Sindhi Phulka (Roti/Chapati) and Bhuga Chawal (Red caramelized rice). A friend found rice bit sweet, but I found it perfect, The Sai Bhaji was super nice.
Mains: Sindhi Kadhi, Rice, one of the friends found it not as Tangy, but the owner later mentioned, we can ask to customize dishes as per taste.
Drinks, we had butter milk and freshlime soda, both were good, the quantity for butter milk was little less, so we ordered more.
Desserts:  Singer ji Mithai, I don’t eat sugar, so I did not taste the sweets, but my friends loved gulab jamun, they said it was exceptional, but the senv mithai was ok ok.

✅ Service: 4/5
When we went there was not much of crowd, so service was good overall, but we had to wait quite a bit for sindhi kadhi and rice.

✅ Ambiance: 5/5  Loved the place, it feels very cozy

✅ Value: We spent about 800 per head, I would totally go here for special occasions, for regular meals, I would want to try thali next time.

featured_reviews.name: RCD thefoodie
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was recently introduced to authentic Sindhi food and I have to admit it’s one of the tastiest delicacies in the list of our Indian cuisines. Not many people are fond of it, cos you hardly have restaurants serving authentic, traditional dishes. But once you get to taste the original varieties you will be highly amazed.
I had a pop up event to attend @ khar and I met some good set of foodie friends over there who were equally excited like me to try out this outlet at khar. As I regularly visit the Lower Parel outlet I was damn sure that my friends would love their food. And as expected warm welcome, fabulous staff and amazing Sindhi menu to choose from.

We ordered:
🔹Beejiya di Tikki - Unique combination of lotus stem along with potatoes tasted so good, not to forget the crispy tangy fritter of lotus stem on top adds to the crunch of this soft tikkis.Highly recommended👍
🔹Kachari- Ab Sindhi restaurant aye aur papad nahi try kiya toh kya kiya?
Well this Modak shaped yummy papad made out of soaked rice is a must try. Highly recommended 👍
🔹Sindhi Pani Puri - So the puris are not crunchy but rather khasta and believe me they literally melt in your mouth and the beautiful flavour of masaledaar aloo stuffing along with sweet and spicy chutney is too good.
🔹Chole Pattice - I wonder why I never tried this dish from their menu. It was our absolute favourite and we ordered for 2 more plates. So basically it was crunchy aloo pattice which was stuffed with spicy Chana dal and served along with perfectly cooked mildly spiced chole which balanced the flavour beautifully, accompanied with pav and green chutney to adjust the spice level as per your liking. Highly recommended 👍
🔹Sindhi Thali - The complete package😜😜
Cos you get to taste so many varieties on a go.
I personally love the combination of bhuga chawal with Sindhi curry and sai bhaji with paratha.
🔹Sev Mithai - Do not leave this place without having their master piece.. Trust me it’s one of the best loaded with ghee and mawa. Highly recommended 👍
🔹Pan Milkshake - Nice and nutty paan flavour, served absolutely chilled.

Overall my girls were super happy as they all stay nearby and thanked me for introducing” Juss by sindhful “ to them 😍

featured_reviews.name: Mrugesh Samel
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is surely one of the best in Mumbai. Simple, authentic regional Indian food prepared using good quality ingredients seems to be their mantra and surely it's working well. Bheeyan ji tikki, Sai bhaji, Sindhi curry, singhar ji mithai are highly recommended here. Do not miss out on this place.

featured_reviews.name: Foodadda Mumbai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Here's an outlet for authentic sindhi food & pure vegans. Our attendant Kuldeep's service was very nice. The staff members were polite and welcoming. It's nearby by Khar station, it  hardly takes 5mins to reach. The ambience is attractive. They have two floors seating section. The wall is painted beautifully with large frame of women in beautiful Indian attire, one side of the wall is full of bronze plates hanging all over the wall and scripts in hindi language, as we go ahead the wall is fully painted it's so beautiful with floral paintings and they have wooden tables, chairs which are very comfortable to seat.

Coming to the food :

In Mocktails (PE-PE-PE) :

Paan Milkshake : This was served in a bottle. The flavour of paan was just heaven. The first sip i took made me feel so refreshed, that i completed this shake in no time.

Mango Lassi : This was also served in a bottle. A mandatory drink in summers. It was tempting and nice as always.

In Appetizers (NASTO) :

Chola Dabla : It was mixture of pav, chole and chat. It was topped with spicy chutneys and curd. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

In Main Course (KHADO) :

Peeli Dal, Bhindi Basar, Steamed Rice And Phulkas :

It was the best combo meal. The best peeli dal I have ever ate, really authentic and delicious in taste. Bhindi basar was the basic bhindi cooked with tomatoes, it also tasted delicious.

Veg Sindhi Thali :

Here before they use you provide unlimited Thali but now they have changed it & keep it as limited one. And if you want you can add Sai Bhaji or Bhuga Chawal but for this you have to pay extra. Also there is option in between 2 Phulkas or 3 Pooris. This thali is really huge. The thali contains about 12 items and each one of the dishes were incredibly delicious. It has.

Aloo Tuk (2pcs)
Sindhi Curry
Paneer Makhani
Bhee Aloo Sabzi
Sai Bhaji
Bhuga Chawal
Steam Rice
2 Phulkas and 2 Pooris
Masala Chass
Kheecha Papad
Boondi Raita
Meetha Lola

In Dessert (KUCH MEETHO) :

Singhar Ji Mithai : This one is our favourite of the lot. And we will go back here just to have this dessert. It was made of sev & milk. It had a little gulkand taste and topped with some almonds. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

Overall a good place, totally worth it. Must visit this place.

featured_reviews.name: Sonali Punjabi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a sindhi and I was looking for someplace very authentic in sindhi taste when I was recommended Juss by sindhful. Juss in sindhi translates to magic, so this was my most awaited!
The food was heavenly. It was typically like “ghar ka khaana”, served really hot and with just the right amount of spices. Oil was minimal and the food was just perfectly cooked. The staff was very helpful and courteous, the the ambiance was very very transitional. I loved every moment I spent there.

featured_reviews.name: Srishti Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text:
The outlet is located at a walking distance from Khar railway station and serves some authentic dishes from Sindhi cuisine. Restaurants serving Sindhi food are very few and this one truly shines as one of the brightest amongst them. They also have good options in North Indian and Chinese food. Ordered the following from here :

Chilli Basil Broccoli & Mushroom - Broccoli and Mushroom sauteed in flavourful gravy, it tasted amazing. Mushroom was soft and the broccoli was a bit hard, the texture contrast was pretty good. Dry gravy was spicy and brought the whole dish together..

Chilli Oyster Chicken - Chunks of tender chicken cooked in oyster sauce with lots of garlic pieces, rendering the dish spicy with just a hint of sweetness. Bell peppers added the crunch in this one and we absolutely loved the flavour of the whole thing..

Chicken Kheema Pav - Looked very mouth-watering and it did deliver in terms of flavour. The quantity was great, considering that we could have easily eaten 6 pavs with the Kheema, but our tummies gave up. It was the right amount of spicy for a Kheema and the chicken was perfectly minced. Pav was soft and the eggs added that little extra..

featured_reviews.name: Nitika Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
We started with the paani puri which was delicious to the core .Super crisp puris stuffed with aaloo & boondi served with 2 types of sweet & tangy water made of imli & mint which was simply heaven . Loved it .

Next we tried the pakwan churra chaat sev puri which had pakwan as base topped wit sev , aaloo & different chutney making it immensely tasty .
It was surprising to enjoy clean , hygenic street style food in a place like kamla mill with foot tapping music , drinks & posh crowd all at highly pocket friendly rates .

We also tried a platter of deep fried sindhi special delicacies including aaloo & arbi tuk , bheeyan ji tikki & sanna pakora . Each of them had a different texture & flavour which was one better than the other & difficult to choose the best . Sprinkled with a lot of spices the freshly ground spices added a strong punch to the starters which we all thoroughly enjoyed .

We simply couldnt resist the temptation to order the special unlimited Sindhi thaali which consisted of rose sherbat , sindhi papad , aaloo tuk , sindhi curry , sindhi mutter paneer , daran ji bhaji , steamed rice , puris & sevai kheer . Every item had an identity of its own & the use of authentic masalas added the homely feel not unlike the regular commercial food available at food courts .
We simply couldnt stop ordering the sevai kheer was it was divine & perfectly balanced in all respect .A complete meal which was simply satisfying in all respect .

Thoroughly enjoyed the entire Sindhi experience .
Daddo Suttho !!!
( means very nice in Sindhi language )

featured_reviews.name: Food Chain Mumbai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Juss by Sindhful is a restaurant which specialises in Sindhi Food as their Main Cuisine and they have got this wall:- wherein you could find most of the famous words, phrases used by Sindhis, like - Dadho Sutho (Very Good), Acho Acho (Come Come), Mathe je Sur (Headache), Charyo Safa (Mad Lad) and many other Sindhi words/phrases, +1 for the quirky ambience.

It's quiet a cozy place and it boasts to be the first restaurant in India to serve unlimited Sindhi thali.

Anyway, let's start about food:-

Recommendations-

• Chole Pattice
• From Thali - Puri with Bhindi Basar, Alu Tuk, Pakoras, Sindhi Kadi with Rice
• Gulab Jamun

• Chole Pattice - 4/5

Heart Shaped Fried Potatoes with Channa embedded in it is served alongside Chole, Onions soaked in Chatni and 2 Luke warm pavs.

The Pattice and Chole tasted good, Pattice was not spicy as you would find the channa embedded in Pattice to be overwhelming at many places, and the Chole, too were not spicy and were rich in flavours.

I liked how they avoided making this classic sindhi dish spicy as it ruins the experience for me.

• Sindhi Unlimited Thali - 4.5/5

This Thali has all the signature sindhi dishes like; bhindi basar, sindhi kadhi, bhugga chawal, sai bhaji, alu tuk, pakoras which is served with rice and puri &/or roti along with Rose sherbet and last but not the least Gulab Jamun.

My favourite among the thali were pakoras, sindhi curry and rice, bhindi basar with puri, pakoras and Alu tuk.

Gulab Jamun served hot and it was topped with almonds. I liked it how Gulab Jamun was not too sweet as many places make the Gulab Jamun too sweet.

• Paan Milkshake & Guava Cooler - 3.5/5

Beverages at Juss are served in a glass bottle with their Branding on it.

Paan Milkshake has the refreshing flavour of Paan but it was little too sweet.

Guava Cooler was fruity and a worthy alternative to your regular Mojito because it is refreshing flavour and since it was mildly sweet, it was a perfect beverage to sip on during the meal.

.

​Great taste, fresh preparation, and completely value for money!

featured_reviews.name: Amol Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for authentic Delhi-style soya chaap in Andheri West, KOALSA Fire Kitchen is definitely a must-visit! Their pure veg menu is a paradise for chaap lovers, bringing the real North Indian street-food experience to Mumbai.

The biggest highlight is their Delhi-style soya chaap—perfectly marinated, juicy, smoky, and grilled with that proper tandoori flavour that instantly reminds you of Delhi NCR street food.

The malai chaap was especially soft, rich, and full of flavour, with that smoky tandoori taste that’s hard to find in Mumbai. Their tandoori chaap and spicy masala chaap also deliver that authentic Delhi-style taste. Along with chaap, their stuffed parathas and North Indian gravy dishes make the menu perfect for a complete meal.

Being completely pure veg makes it even better for families and vegetarian food lovers. Their tandoori dishes, creamy gravies, and chaap preparations are packed with flavour and give that proper “Delhi wala taste” that’s truly hard to find here.

Highly recommended for anyone who loves rich North Indian flavours and authentic Delhi-style soya chaap!

1. Paneer Chilli- This one was the yummiest out of the whole menu. The paneer was quiet soft and springy and was well marinated in the soy sauce and chillies.
2. Veg Seekh kebab- It was basically a potato seekh roll kebab. It was okayish in taste but had a very dry mouth feel.would taste good with sauce.
3.Subz Dum Biryani- It was same as the regular dum Biryanis and was served with complimentary raita and green chutney which added more flavour when had together with the Biryani.The veggies in the biryani were well cooked.
4. Triple schezwan fried Rice - Chinese has always been my favorite cuisine hence something from the menu had to be Chinese so ordered this. The rice along with the gravy tasted yumm!
Personally I had a good experience. The service,food, packaging everything was good . The only thing they need to have more consideration on is their outlet and the kitchens hygiene. Would still recommend this outlet for a one time visit for sure!

featured_reviews.name: ReservedSeat
featured_reviews.review_text:
A really nice place to order food from if you happen to be a big fan of desi chinese. Although this takeout joint serves both Mughlai and Chinese food, we prefer the chinese here for its has great taste and amazing portion size.

While we have called a lot of times from this joint, the dishes we would highly like to recommend the next time you order your take out, it is Paneer Singapuri for starters, Paneer In Manchurian Sauce as mains in gravy, Veg Triple Schezwan Fried Rice because no desi chinese meal is complete without it and Veg Hongkong Noodles.

What also works for this take out joint is that it delivers till wee hours in the morning so you definitely don't have to worry about late night cravings or call in for food when you have friends over for a night party.
